Reproduced for legal-awareness purposes.] ======================================================================== PREAMBLE ======================================================================== The Contracting Parties, desiring to facilitate international road traffic and to increase road safety through the adoption of uniform traffic rules, have agreed as follows:

adoption of uniform traffic rules, have agreed as follows: ======================================================================== CHAPTER I  GENERAL PROVISIONS ======================================================================== Article 1  Definitions For the purposes of this Convention, the following expressions shall have the meanings hereby assigned to them: (a) "domestic legislation"

hereby assigned to them: (a) "domestic legislation" means the complete body of national or local laws and regulations in force in the territory of a Contracting Party; (b) "built-up area" means an area with entries and exits specially signposted as such, or otherwise defined in domestic legislation; (c) "road" means the entire width of any way or street open to public motor traffic; (d)

of any way or street open to public motor traffic; (d) "carriageway" means the part of a road normally used by vehicular traffic; a road may have several carriageways; (e) "lane" means any one of the longitudinal strips into which the carriageway is divisible; (f) "intersection" means any level crossing of roads, junction or bifurcation, including the open areas formed by such crossings,

including the open areas formed by such crossings, junctions or bifurcations; (g) "level crossing" means any level intersection between a road and a railway or tramway track with its own track formation; (h) "motorway" means a road specially designed and built for motor traffic, which does not serve properties bordering on it, which is provided with separate carriageways for the two directions of

with separate carriageways for the two directions of traffic separated by a dividing strip not intended for traffic or by another means, which has no level crossing with any road, railway or tramway track, or footpath, and which is specifically signposted as a motorway; (i) "vehicle" means any conveyance, including a power-driven vehicle, travelling on a road; (j) "power-driven vehicle" means any

travelling on a road; (j) "power-driven vehicle" means any self-propelled road vehicle other than those which run on rails; this term also covers mopeds; (k) "motor vehicle" means any power-driven vehicle which is normally used for carrying persons or goods by road or for drawing, on the road, vehicles used for the carriage of persons or goods; the term covers trolley buses, i.e., vehicles

or goods; the term covers trolley buses, i.e., vehicles connected to an electric conductor and not running on rails; (l) "trailer" means any vehicle designed to be drawn by a power-driven vehicle; the term covers semi-trailers; (m) "semi-trailer" means any trailer designed to be coupled to a motor vehicle in such a way that part of it rests on the motor vehicle and a substantial part of its

it rests on the motor vehicle and a substantial part of its weight and of the weight of its load is borne by the motor vehicle; (n) "cycle" means any vehicle which has at least two wheels and is propelled solely by the muscular energy of the persons on that vehicle, in particular by means of pedals or hand-cranks; (o) "moped" means any two-wheeled or three-wheeled vehicle which is fitted with an

or three-wheeled vehicle which is fitted with an internal combustion engine having a cylinder capacity not exceeding 50 cc (3.05 cu.in.) and a maximum design speed not exceeding 50 km (31 miles) per hour; (p) "motorcycle" means any two-wheeled vehicle with or without a sidecar, fitted with a power unit; mopeds are not included if domestic legislation classifies them as cycles; (q) "driver" means

legislation classifies them as cycles; (q) "driver" means any person who drives a vehicle, including cycles, or who guides cattle, singly or in herds, or flocks, or draught, pack or saddle animals on a road; (r) "permissible maximum mass" means the maximum mass of the laden vehicle declared permissible by the competent authority of the State in which the vehicle is registered; (s) "direction of

State in which the vehicle is registered; (s) "direction of traffic" and "appropriate" (as applied to a side of the road) means the right-hand side if, under domestic legislation, the driver must pass the oncoming traffic on his left; and the left-hand side if, under domestic legislation, the driver must pass the oncoming traffic on his right; (t) "priority" means the right to pass before another
(t) "priority" means the right to pass before another road-user

. Article 2  Annexes to the Convention The following Annexes are attached to this Convention and form an integral part thereof: Annex 1: Exceptions from the obligation to admit motor vehicles and trailers in international traffic Annex 2: Registration number of motor vehicles and trailers in international traffic Annex 3: Distinguishing sign of motor vehicles and trailers in international traffic

of motor vehicles and trailers in international traffic Annex 4: Identification marks of motor vehicles and trailers in international traffic Annex 5: Technical conditions concerning motor vehicles and trailers Annex 6: Domestic driving permit Annex 7: International Driving Permit Article 3  Obligations of Contracting Parties 1

. (a) Contracting Parties shall take appropriate measures to ensure that the rules of road traffic in force in their territories conform, in substance, to the provisions of Chapter II of this Convention

. (b) Contracting Parties shall also take appropriate measures to ensure that the rules of road traffic in force in their territories with respect to the technical conditions which motor vehicles and trailers must satisfy conform to the provisions of Annex 5 to this Convention

. (c) Subject to the exceptions provided for in Annex 1, Contracting Parties shall be bound to admit to their territories in international traffic motor vehicles and trailers which fulfil the conditions laid down in Chapter III of this Convention and whose drivers fulfil the conditions laid down in Chapter IV

. Article 4  Signs and Signals Contracting Parties shall, unless they have already done so, take the necessary measures to conform, within the time-limits specified therein, to the provisions of the Protocol on Road Signs and Signals opened for signature at Geneva on 19 September 1949, or to the Convention on Road Signs and Signals opened for signature at Vienna on 8 November 1968

. ======================================================================== CHAPTER II  RULES OF THE ROAD ======================================================================== Article 5  Force of Signs and Signals 1. Road users shall comply with the instructions conveyed by road signs, road markings and traffic light signals, even if those instructions appear to conflict with other traffic rules

. 2. Instructions conveyed by traffic light signals shall take precedence over those conveyed by road signs giving priority. Article 6  Instructions given by Authorized Officials 1. Road users shall comply immediately with any instruction given by officials duly authorized for that purpose by the competent authority, in particular by police officers. 2

. 2. Road users shall also comply with instructions given by flagmen or other persons authorized to control traffic at roadworks, level crossings, airports, public events and similar circumstances. Article 7  General Rules 1. Road users shall avoid any behaviour likely to endanger or obstruct traffic, to endanger persons, or to cause damage to public or private property. 2

. 2. It is recommended that domestic legislation should provide that road users shall not endanger or unnecessarily obstruct traffic. 3. Drivers shall be in a fit state to drive and shall have adequate knowledge and skills; however, the physical and mental fitness to drive and the level of knowledge and skills required shall be determined by domestic legislation. 4

. 4. Drivers of power-driven vehicles shall have the skills required for driving and shall have adequate knowledge of traffic rules. This requirement does not prejudice the right of persons to learn to drive in accordance with domestic legislation. Article 8  Driver of Vehicle 1. Every moving vehicle or combination of vehicles shall have a driver. 2

. 2. It is recommended that domestic legislation should provide that pack, draught or saddle animals and livestock shall be driven by a driver. 3. Every driver shall at all times be able to control his vehicle or to guide his animals. 4. A driver of a motor vehicle shall at all times ensure that he can see ahead, to the right and to the left sufficiently well for safety. 5

. 5. Every driver of a vehicle shall at all times ensure that his vehicle or its load does not prevent him from seeing sufficiently well, that it does not endanger road users or the public and does not damage public or private property

. Article 9  Flocks and Herds It is recommended that domestic legislation should provide that livestock shall as far as possible be kept to the side of the road and that if their number exceeds a certain figure they shall be divided into groups of limited size with sufficient space between groups to allow traffic to pass. Article 10  Position on the Carriageway 1
. Article 10  Position on the Carriageway 1. The direction of traffic shall be the same throughout the territory of each Contracting Party and on all roads in that territory. 2

. 2. On roads with two or more lanes in the direction of travel, drivers shall not use the lane nearest to the edge of the carriageway appropriate to the oncoming traffic except to the extent necessary to pass parked vehicles or vehicles moving in the same direction as themselves; this restriction shall not apply when it is needed to prevent accidents. 3

. 3. When a driver is on a carriageway where the lanes are marked, he shall ensure that the vehicle remains in the lane he has chosen and shall only change lanes after having ascertained that he can do so without risk to himself or to other road users and after giving the prescribed signal. Article 11  Overtaking and Passing 1. Overtaking shall be on the side away from the direction of traffic

. Where lanes are marked on the carriageway, overtaking may be done on the right if the driver has chosen a lane to the left of another lane used by a vehicle he intends to overtake, or on the left if the driver has chosen a lane to the right. 2

. Before overtaking, every driver shall, without prejudice to the provisions of Article 7, paragraph 1, and to those of Article 14, make sure: (a) that no driver who is following him has begun to overtake him; (b) that the driver ahead of him in the same lane has not signalled his intention to overtake another vehicle; (c) that the gap between him and the oncoming traffic is sufficient for him to

him and the oncoming traffic is sufficient for him to overtake without endangering oncoming traffic, taking into account his speed and the speed of the vehicles being overtaken and the road conditions

. 3. In application of the provisions of paragraph 2 of this Article, it is forbidden to overtake: (a) at or approaching intersections and at or approaching level crossings without gates or barriers; (b) at or approaching the crest of a hill and, where visibility is insufficient, on bends; (c) in any other places of restricted visibility. 4
. 4. The driver of an overtaken vehicle shall reduce his speed if necessary to enable the overtaking vehicle to clear it, and shall not accelerate while being overtaken

. Article 12  Keeping to the Right (or to the Appropriate Side) The driver of a vehicle meeting an oncoming vehicle shall move to the appropriate side; if in so doing he runs the risk of moving onto the shoulder or of leaving the carriageway, he may reduce his speed and if necessary stop. Article 13  Speed and Distance Between Vehicles 1

. Article 13  Speed and Distance Between Vehicles 1. Every driver of a vehicle shall in all circumstances have his vehicle under control so as to be able to exercise due and proper care and to react in time to any foreseeable event. 2

. 2. Every driver shall keep to a reasonable speed, and if he sees that the speed limit prescribed by domestic legislation is about to be exceeded or if this would constitute a danger to the traffic on the road in question, he shall slow down and if necessary stop his vehicle. 3. The speed limit applicable on the road being used shall be observed. 4

. 4. At night and in conditions of poor visibility, drivers shall adjust their speed to the limits of their headlight illumination. 5. Every driver of a vehicle following another vehicle shall keep at a sufficient distance from that other vehicle to avoid a collision if the vehicle in front should suddenly slow down or stop. Article 14  Priority 1

. Article 14  Priority 1. Every driver approaching an intersection shall exercise such care as may be required by the local conditions. 2. A driver who is not on a priority road shall yield right of way to vehicles travelling on the priority road. 3

. 3. Subject to the provisions of paragraph 2 of this Article, vehicles shall at intersections yield right of way to vehicles approaching from their right, unless domestic legislation establishes a different rule. 4

. 4. The principle of yielding right of way to vehicles from the right, even if not a statutory rule, is widely applied in signatory states and should be assumed by drivers unfamiliar with local rules

. Article 15  Special Rules Applicable to Authorized Emergency Vehicles Domestic legislation shall make provision for special rules regarding the priority of duly authorized vehicles in service on urgent duty and identifiable as such. Article 16  Changing Direction 1

. Before turning right or left for the purpose of entering another road or entering a property bordering on the road, every driver shall: (a) if he wishes to turn off on the side appropriate to the direction of traffic, keep as close as possible to that edge of the carriageway; (b) if he wishes to turn off on the other side, move as close as possible to the centre of the carriageway and, if he is

as possible to the centre of the carriageway and, if he is leaving a road on which traffic moves in both directions to enter another such road, make the turn in such a way as to join the carriageway of the road he is entering on the appropriate side

. 2. While changing direction, the driver shall yield right of way to vehicles meeting him on the road he is about to enter and to cyclists and moped riders moving along that road. Article 17  Slowing Down Every driver intending to slow down shall, unless the slow-down is imperceptible, first make sure that he can do so without risk or inconvenience to other drivers

. He shall give warning of his intention unless he has good reason for not doing so. Article 18  Intersections and Obligation to Give Way 1. At every road intersection, a driver coming from a road giving priority shall give way to vehicles coming from a priority road or to vehicles which, by virtue of the regulation governing priority at that intersection, have the right to cross first. 2

. 2. At intersections other than those governed by a give-way sign or by traffic signals, drivers shall give way to vehicles coming from their right. 3. At intersections between roads of different relative importance determined by road signs and at intersections where rules of priority are in force, every driver shall obey those rules
. Article 19  Level Crossings Road users shall exercise particular care at level crossings

. In particular: (a) every driver of a vehicle shall approach a level crossing at a moderate speed and shall not cross the railway track unless he can see that no train or other rail vehicle is approaching; (b) in particular, drivers shall not start to cross a level crossing when the crossing gate is closed or being closed, or when the red lights flash or the bell rings or rings repeatedly

. Article 20  Rules Applicable to Pedestrians 1. If there are pavements or footpaths on a road, pedestrians shall use them. Nevertheless, pedestrians pushing a cycle, a moped, or a motorcycle, pedestrians pushing or carrying bulky objects, groups of pedestrians being conducted by a person responsible for them, and processions shall be permitted to use the carriageway. 2

. 2. If there are no pavements or footpaths, or if it is impracticable to use them, pedestrians may walk on the carriageway; where there is a cycle track and its use by pedestrians is not prohibited by domestic legislation, pedestrians may use it, but shall not obstruct cycle or moped traffic. 3. Pedestrians walking on the carriageway shall keep as close as possible to the edge of the carriageway

. 4. Pedestrians crossing a carriageway shall do so with caution; before stepping on to the carriageway, they shall make sure that they can do so without danger. 5. Pedestrians shall not cross a carriageway at an intersection where traffic is controlled by traffic light signals, except when the traffic light signal for pedestrians shows that they may cross. 6

. 6. Pedestrians shall cross the carriageway perpendicular to its axis, either at pedestrian crossings, if any exist nearby, or at intersections, or along a straight line if crossings and intersections are too far away. Article 21  Behaviour of Drivers towards Pedestrians 1

. Article 21  Behaviour of Drivers towards Pedestrians 1. Notwithstanding the provisions of Article 18, paragraph 1 of this Convention, every driver shall, where necessary to ensure the safety of pedestrians, yield right of way to pedestrians who have already stepped on to or who are about to step on to a pedestrian crossing marked on the carriageway by signs or road markings. 2

. 2. Drivers shall not endanger pedestrians by swerving or by driving with undue speed near a pedestrian crossing. 3. Drivers shall not overtake another vehicle immediately before a pedestrian crossing. Article 22  Rules Applicable to Cyclists 1

. Article 22  Rules Applicable to Cyclists 1. It is recommended that domestic legislation should provide that cyclists shall not ride without holding the handlebars, shall not allow themselves to be towed by another vehicle, and shall not carry, tow or push loads or other persons in such a way as to endanger their safety or to be a nuisance to other road users. 2

. 2. It is recommended that domestic legislation should also provide that cyclists shall not ride side by side on the carriageway except on paths or parts of the road reserved for cyclists. Article 23  Stopping and Parking 1. Outside built-up areas, vehicles, when stopped or parked, shall be placed outside the carriageway if possible

. Whether or not they are placed on the carriageway, stopped or parked vehicles shall, if possible, be placed on the side appropriate to the direction of traffic. 2. Vehicles shall not be stopped or parked in a dangerous position or in such circumstances as to create a danger or obstacle for traffic. 3

. 3. In particular, in built-up areas, if no parking is indicated by road signs or road markings, every driver shall take care not to cause inconvenience to the movement of other vehicles or pedestrians. Article 24  Opening of Doors No person shall open the door of a vehicle, leave it open, or get out of the vehicle without having made sure that he cannot thereby endanger other road users
. Article 25  Motorways and Similar Roads 1

. On motorways and, if domestic legislation so provides, on specially signposted fast-traffic roads: (a) the use of the road by pedestrians, animals, cycles, mopeds and all vehicles other than motor vehicles and their trailers, and by motor vehicles or trailers which cannot, by virtue of their design, exceed a set speed on a level road, shall be prohibited; (b) drivers shall not make U-turns,
shall be prohibited; (b) drivers shall not make U-turns, shall not drive in reverse, and shall not cross the central dividing strip, including gaps in it

. 2. Drivers shall not stop or park on motorways except at specially designated parking areas. If a vehicle is immobilized on the carriageway or hard shoulder owing to a breakdown, the driver shall try to move it off the carriageway as soon as possible and shall place the prescribed warning device at an appropriate distance from the vehicle in order to warn approaching traffic. 3

. 3. Drivers using a motorway shall join it only from the right (or left in countries with left-hand traffic) by means of the approach roads. They shall leave by the appropriate exit roads. Article 26  Special Rules Applicable to Convoys Special rules may be laid down in domestic legislation for traffic convoys

. A convoy may not be overtaken or separated by other vehicles when it is moving as a unit with its headlights on and announced by auditory warning. Article 27  Special Rules Applicable to Cyclists, Moped Riders and Motorcyclists 1

. It is recommended that domestic legislation should provide that cyclists shall use only roads and sections of roads designated for them or, failing this, as close to the edge of the carriageway as possible. 2. The provisions of paragraph 1 of this Article shall apply to moped riders where domestic legislation so provides. 3

. 3. Motorcyclists and moped riders shall not hold on to another vehicle in motion. Article 28  Auditory and Luminous Warnings 1. Auditory warning devices may be used only to give warning in order to avoid an accident. 2

. 2. Drivers of motor vehicles shall use dipped headlights or, if the motor vehicle is not equipped with dipped headlights, some other appropriate light, when driving in built-up areas at night. 3. Drivers shall use dipped headlights when overtaking in built-up areas at night and when visibility is adversely affected. 4

. 4. Outside built-up areas, drivers shall use main-beam headlights in the absence of adequate road lighting. They shall switch to dipped headlights when meeting oncoming vehicles and when following another vehicle. Article 29  Rail-Borne Vehicles On roads used by both rail-borne vehicles and other road users, the latter shall give way to the rail-borne vehicles. Article 30  Loading of Vehicles 1

. The load of a vehicle shall be so arranged and, if necessary, stowed that: (a) it cannot endanger persons, damage public or private property, or cause nuisance (e.g., through noise, dust, smell); (b) it does not obstruct the driver's view or impair the stability or driving of the vehicle; (c) it does not obscure the lights or the distinguishing and registration marks of the vehicle
. Article 31  Behaviour After an Accident 1. Every driver or other road user involved in a road accident shall stop as soon as he can do so without causing a further danger to traffic. 2

. 2. If a road accident results in injury, every driver or other road user involved shall: (a) take or have taken all measures at his disposal to ensure the safety of traffic and, if a person is killed or seriously injured, to avoid, in so far as possible, any action that would make it more difficult to establish what happened; (b) inform the police or other competent authorities. 3

. 3. If a road accident involves only damage to property, every driver or other road user involved shall take all measures at his disposal to avoid danger to other road users. 4. Contracting Parties may, in their domestic legislation, require persons involved in a road accident to give their name and address to other persons involved. 5
. 5. If a road accident results in injury or death, Contracting Parties shall require that the facts of the accident be reported to the police

. ======================================================================== CHAPTER III  CONDITIONS FOR ADMISSION OF MOTOR VEHICLES AND TRAILERS TO INTERNATIONAL TRAFFIC ======================================================================== Article 36  Registration 1

. In order to be admissible to international traffic, every motor vehicle and every trailer coupled to a motor vehicle shall: (a) be registered by a Contracting Party and bear a registration number; (b) display at the rear, if it is a motor vehicle, its registration number, and if it is a trailer, its registration number or, where it is permitted by the legislation of the Contracting Party in

is permitted by the legislation of the Contracting Party in whose territory the vehicle is registered, the registration number of the towing vehicle; (c) display at the rear the distinguishing sign of the State in whose territory it is registered

. 2. A Contracting Party may refuse to admit to international traffic on its territory any motor vehicle or trailer which does not comply with the requirements of the present Convention. Article 37  Technical Conditions 1. Motor vehicles admitted to international traffic shall satisfy the technical conditions laid down in Annex 5 to this Convention. 2

. 2. Trailers admitted to international traffic shall satisfy the technical conditions laid down in Annex 5 to this Convention. Article 38  Lighting and Light-Signalling Devices Motor vehicles shall be equipped with lighting and light-signalling devices in accordance with the requirements of Annex 5

. Article 39  Rear View Mirror and Windscreen Wipers Every motor vehicle shall be equipped with at least one rear-view mirror and, if it has a windscreen, with a windscreen wiper. Article 41  International Driving Permit 1

. Article 41  International Driving Permit 1. An international driving permit shall be issued in accordance with the provisions of Annex 7 by a Contracting Party or by an association duly authorized by that Contracting Party. 2

. 2. The international driving permit shall be valid for a maximum period of three years from the date of issue or until the domestic driving permit on which it is based expires, whichever is the shorter period

. ======================================================================== CHAPTER IV  DRIVERS OF MOTOR VEHICLES ======================================================================== Article 41  Driving Licences 1. Contracting Parties shall require every driver of a motor vehicle to hold a driving licence

. Each Contracting Party shall recognize: (a) any domestic driving permit issued in any other Contracting Party, or (b) any international driving permit, as authorizing the holder to drive in its territory vehicles of the category shown in those permits. 2

. 2. A domestic driving permit shall be recognized in the territory of any Contracting Party until the document has expired or the holder has established his normal residence in that territory. 3. Driving licences shall be issued only after a driving test; the conditions of admission to the driving test shall be determined by domestic legislation. 4

. 4. Every Contracting Party shall have the right not to recognize the validity of driving permits issued to persons who, at the time they were issued, had their normal residence in the territory of that Contracting Party. Article 42  Suspension of Validity of Driving Permits 1

. Article 42  Suspension of Validity of Driving Permits 1. Contracting Parties may withdraw from a driver the right to use his domestic or international driving permit in their territory, if he has committed in their territory an offence disqualifying him from driving under their domestic legislation. 2

. 2. Contracting Parties may withdraw from a driver the right to use his domestic or international driving permit in their territory if he has committed abroad an offence that would disqualify him from driving under their domestic legislation

. ======================================================================== ANNEX 5  TECHNICAL CONDITIONS CONCERNING MOTOR VEHICLES AND TRAILERS (Key provisions) ======================================================================== Section 1  Braking Every motor vehicle shall be equipped with a braking system which will be effective on any gradient, in all loading conditions and at any speed the

gradient, in all loading conditions and at any speed the motor vehicle can achieve, and which enables the driver to control the motor vehicle safely and to reduce its speed or stop it in emergency situations

. Section 2  Lighting Every motor vehicle shall be equipped with: (a) two white or yellow front-position (side) lights; (b) two red rear-position (tail) lights; (c) two red stop-lights which can be seen by day and night; (d) two white reversing lights (recommended); (e) direction indicators at the front and rear; (f) one white or yellow front fog lamp and one red rear fog lamp (required in bad
front fog lamp and one red rear fog lamp (required in bad weather)

. Section 3  Tyres Tyres shall be of a type appropriate for the use to which the vehicle is put, shall not be worn to the extent that the tread pattern is indistinguishable, and shall comply with the minimum tread-depth requirements set by domestic legislation (typically 1.6 mm across the central three-quarters of the tread width and around the entire circumference)

. Section 4  Speed Limiter Heavy goods vehicles and buses admitted to international traffic are recommended to be fitted with a speed limiter that prevents the vehicle from exceeding the maximum speed prescribed for that category in the Contracting Parties' domestic legislation

. ======================================================================== ANNEX 6  DOMESTIC DRIVING PERMIT (Key provisions) ======================================================================== The domestic driving permit shall show: 1. The distinguishing sign of the Contracting Party which issued it. 2. The title of the permit in the national language(s) of the Contracting Party. 3

. 3. The surname, first name(s), and date of birth of the holder. 4. The date of issue and the date of expiry of the permit. 5. The authority that issued the permit. 6. The categories of vehicles the holder is authorized to drive, in accordance with the categories defined in this Convention

. ======================================================================== ANNEX 7  INTERNATIONAL DRIVING PERMIT (Key provisions) ======================================================================== 1. The International Driving Permit (IDP) is valid only when accompanied by the domestic driving permit to which it relates. 2

. 2. The IDP shall be printed in French, with translations in English, Russian, Spanish, Arabic, and Chinese. 3. The holder of the IDP is authorized to drive in all Contracting Parties the categories of vehicle for which the IDP has been issued, subject to any restrictions noted on the permit. 4

. 4. The IDP does not replace the need for local insurance or compliance with domestic traffic regulations of the host Contracting Party. ======================================================================== KEY PRINCIPLES APPLICABLE TO ALL SIGNATORY NATIONS (Summary for DriveLegal users) ======================================================================== 1

. DRIVING SIDE: Each country chooses the side of the road (left or right), and this applies uniformly throughout its territory. As a visitor, you must observe the host country's rule. 2. SPEED: Obey posted speed limits. In the absence of a posted limit, general limits in built-up areas typically range from 3050 km/h; outside built-up areas from 80100 km/h; on motorways from 100130 km/h

. Exact limits differ by country. 3. ALCOHOL: Most signatory states set a blood-alcohol concentration (BAC) limit of 0.05 g/dl (50 mg/100 ml) or lower. Some apply 0.00 g/dl to new or professional drivers. Violation is a serious offence in all signatories. 4. PRIORITY TO THE RIGHT: At unmarked intersections, give way to vehicles approaching from the right (in right-hand traffic countries)

. This rule applies unless overridden by a road sign. 5. PEDESTRIAN CROSSINGS: Drivers must give way to pedestrians at marked pedestrian crossings, even where no traffic light is present. 6. OVERTAKING: Overtake on the side away from oncoming traffic. Do not overtake at or near intersections, level crossings, hilltops, or bends. 7

. 7. HEADLIGHTS: Use dipped headlights in poor visibility, at night in built-up areas, and when meeting oncoming vehicles. 8. ACCIDENTS: Stop immediately. Assist injured persons. Report to police if injury or death occurred. 9. DRIVING LICENCE: Foreign visitors driving on a domestic licence must carry that licence

. An International Driving Permit (IDP) is required in many signatory states when using a domestic licence issued in a non-signatory country or a licence not in Latin script. 10. VEHICLE CONDITION: The vehicle must meet roadworthiness standards of the host country (lighting, brakes, tyres, reflectors) and display valid registration marks
. [End of Vienna Convention on Road Traffic  DriveLegal corpus extract]
